articleTitle: Weather Forecasting Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The activities of many primary sectors depend on the weather for production, e.g. farming. The climate is changing at a drastic rate nowadays, which makes the old weather prediction methods less effective and more hectic. To overcome these difficulties, the improved and reliable weather prediction methods are required. These predictions affect a nation's economy and the lives of people. To develop a weather forecasting system that can be used in remote areas is the main motivation of this work. The data analytics and machine learning algorithms, such as random forest classification, are used to predict weather conditions. In this paper, a low-cost and portable solution for weather prediction is devised.

articleTitle: Mining Twitter Data for Depression Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Health care twitter analysis deals with the health related tweets through sentimental analysis by the patients themselves. The application of sentiment analysis has grown enormously. Its application in health care has great potential to analyze and improve the health of a country. In this paper, we try to analyze health tweets for Depression, Anxiety from the mixed tweets by using Multinomial Naive Bayes and Support Vector Regression (SVR) Algorithm as a classifier.

articleTitle: Speaker's Voice Characteristics and Similarity Measurement using Euclidean Distances
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The Euclidean distance and MFCC feature extraction technique are the composite way and useful for successfully measure the similarity between speakers. This type of approaches is used in the forensic statics for similarity of voice measurement. The speaker voice similarity is measured by using Euclidean distance (ED) through a different set of speakers as same-same speakers (SS) and difference speakers (DS). This approaches suggested that the feature coefficient of speech maximum dependent on speakers voice. The ED is calculated from the mean of Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) for speaker similarity measurement. There is ED difference method is proposed for finding the similarity index between SS and DS.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Price Forecasting using LSTM and 10-Fold Cross validation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research paper reports the proposed model for price prediction of the popular Bitcoin crypto currency while applying different neural network approaches namely Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) along with 10-fold cross validation. In this work, the analysis of various trends of Bitcoin market is carried out and learning of important features used for price prediction is done. Daily price change is estimated by the neural network models. New activation functions are utilized in this research paper for improving efficiency. Further, this research paper compares the proposed model with other existing models namely; RNN with LSTM, Linear Regression and Random Forest applied in the same domain. The dataset utilized in this work is taken from the website named coinmarket and live streaming data is considered for the experimental work. Keras, Tensorflow and Scikit Learn have been used for performing the experimental work of the proposed model. The performance analysis of the proposed model with the existing ones has been carried out in terms of the Mean Absolute Error (MAE). It is observed from the results retrieved as a part of this work that the MAE for the proposed model came out to be 0.0043s which was significantly less than its existing counterparts.

articleTitle: A Review on Frequency Selective Surfaces and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article presents the frequency selective surfaces (FSS) and its concepts. Principle of operation of FSS is briefly explained. To understand the physical geometry, equivalent circuit models are discussed. Various applications of FSS are studied. It is observed that the FSS have spatial filtering properties and can be implemented as a bandpass or bandstop filter with least attenuation of 20dB. The miniaturized FSS provides angular stability up to 85°. FSS integrated with MIMO antenna system reduces the mutual coupling effect with ECC less than 5e-6 can be obtained. FSS when integrated with the antenna enhances the gain. FSS also provides better electromagnetic shielding. Apart from these, 3D FSS structures and reconfigurable FSS are also discussed. The latest techniques to implement FSS are outlined. The new advancements in this field are also investigated.

articleTitle: Tunnel Field Effect Transistor for Ultra Low Power Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (TFET) has emerged as a promising candidate for applications in low power VLSI/ULSI circuit design. TFETs have shown better performance in terms of short-channel effects and random dopant fluctuation etc as compared to the MOSFET. TFETs are based upon the concept of gated p-i-n diode and band to band tunneling phenomenon. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of TFETs and its performance variation with different parameters. The work also demonstrates the different advancements in TFETs to make it more reliable and cost effective in terms of lower subthreshold swing, higher on-current, lower leakage current, lower DIBL effect and ambipolar current etc. Finally, a comparison between different kinds of advanced TFETs as- doped/ undoped, symmetrical/ asymmetrical and single/double gate TFETs is presented in this work.

articleTitle: Helmet Detection Using ML & IoT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper is about detecting two-wheeler riders without helmet with the help of machine learning and provide them with a user interface to pay challans. The proposed approach first captures the real time image of road traffic and then differentiates the two wheelers from other vehicles in the road. It then processes to check whether the rider and pillion rider are wearing helmet or not using OpenCV. If any one of the riders and pillion rider found not wearing the helmet, their vehicle number plate is processed using optical character recognition (OCR). After extracting the vehicle registration number, a challan will be generated against respective vehicle and all the details of the challan will be sent via E-mail and SMS to the concerned person. An user interface (an app and a website) will also be provided to pay their challans.

articleTitle: Crowdsourcing of Hate Speech for Detecting Abusive Behavior on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Micro blogging sites nowadays provide a platform for a person to express their thoughts and opinions without risking anything. These social media platforms do not provide any religious or political restrictions for the user to restrict them from saying what they want. People use such platforms to express their opinions on current affairs, political campaigns, day to day activities, sports, and other services. One such platform is Twitter. This paper aims at targeting the tweets shared on twitter on the basis of emotion behind them-whether it falls under the category of hate speech or not. This paper identifies hate speech by employing various machine learning algorithms. The paper also derives the context in which various words are used and based on it identifies hate speech. It tries to keep the idea of freedom of speech intact and at the same time curtail hate speech which various other algorithms have failed to do. This paper focuses on applying the hate speech check on anti-national tweets. This can help in marking the users and to demote them to engage in such activities.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Broadband Reflector for Passive Radiative Cooling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a multilayer structure is proposed to design a broadband reflector that has the capability to reflect a wide range of spectrum from ultra-violet to infra-red region for TE polarised light. The design analysis is carried out using transfer matrix method (TMM). The structure is designed using alternate layers of appropriate high and low refractive indices. The proposed structure demonstrates more than 97% reflectivity for the wavelength range of 0.3μm-2.5μm (solar spectrum). Thus, it has the potential to be used in various applications such as passive radiative cooler, and as a heliostat in concentrated solar power etc.

articleTitle: Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles: Restoration of the Network for Next Generation (5G) Optical Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract:
Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles

"Restoration of the Network for Next Generation (5G) Optical Communication Network"
by D. Kumar, Ashutosh Sharma, Rajiv Kumar and Neeru Sharma in the Proceedings of the International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC), 2019

After careful and considered review of the content and authorship of this paper by a duly constituted expert committee, this paper has been found to be in violation of IEEE’s Publication Principles.

This paper copied large portions of text from the paper cited below. The original text was copied without attribution (including appropriate references to the original author(s) and/or paper title) and without permission.

"Network Restoration for Next-Generation Communication and Computing Networks"
by B. S. Awoyemi, A. S. Alfa, and B. T. Maharaj in the Journal of Computer Networks and Communications, 2018


In modern communication network unwanted failures occurred. A design of robust network is required to handle the failures, restore the failed part and maintain the traffic flow of the network within a permissible time frame, at the lowest cost. The next-generation (5G) communication and computing networks, software-defined networks and internet-of-things networks assures to provide high speeds, impressive data rates and remarkable reliability. We need to design complex and robust next generation networks that must be built with minimum failure possibilities, quick failure recovery capabilities and high network restoration capacity. Therefore, improved network restoration models are needs to be developed and incorporated. In this paper, a comprehensive study on network restoration mechanisms that are being developed for addressing network failures in current and next generation (5G) networks is carried out. Open-ended problems are identified, while invaluable ideas for better adaptation of network restoration to evolving 5G communication and computing models are discussed.

articleTitle: Mood Based Music Player
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The ability of music to produce an emotional response in its listeners is one of its most exciting and yet the least understood property. Music not only conveys emotion and meaning but can also stir a listener's mood. This paper will study various algorithms based on classification to provide a clear methodology to i) classify songs into 4 mood categories and ii) detect users mood through his facial expressions and then combine the two to generate user customized music playlist. Songs have been classified by two approaches; by directly training the models namely KNN, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest and MLP using selected audio features and by predicting a songs arousal and valence values using these audio features. The first approach attains maximum accuracy of 70% using MLP while the latter achieves accuracy of 81.6% using SVM regression. The face mood classifier using HAAR classifier and fisher face algorithm attains precision of 92%.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT) Based Smart Shopping Centre Using RFID
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this work, an Internet of Things (IoT) based new Smart Shopping Centre has been proposed using RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) system which aims at assisting the customer while shopping and saving the time and energy spent during it, avoiding the huge rush and long queues. The aim is to simplify and accelerate the process by the use of RFID tags on each product and a device consisting of a Microcontroller, RFID Reader, and Android application connected to the microcontroller using a Bluetooth module. Thus, the proposed work reduces the shopping time of customer by finding the products and waiting at the end in long queues for bill generation and bill payment.

articleTitle: Simulation of MIMO-FSO System with Gamma-Gamma Fading under Different Atmospheric Turbulence Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The performance of Free Space Optics (FSO) based communication systems is mainly degraded by the presence of atmospheric turbulence conditions like haze and rain etc. For performance enhancement the diversity techniques have been used. In this paper, Diversity based FSO / MIMO-FSO systems have been designed to carry out the detailed performance analysis with Gamma-Gamma fading under different Atmospheric Turbulence Conditions such as Clear Weather, Haze and Rain. The MIMO-FSO systems are simulated for diversity / MIMO order 1, 2, 4 and 8 at a high bit rate of 10 Gbps and are compared in terms of Min. BER, Q-Factor, Received Signal Power values using Graphs and Eye Diagrams. The system performance was also analyzed as a function of Beam Divergence, Transmitted Source Power, Receiver Aperture Diameter, FSO Channel Length and Bit Rate. Simulation results depict that MIMO-FSO system performs very well under turbulence conditions even with low optical level of 10 dBm without much distortion up to a sufficiently long distance with increased reliability.

articleTitle: DoG Based Local Ternary Pattern for Image Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel pattern-based feature is proposed for the purpose of image retrieval. It extracts edge information of images using difference of Gaussian (DoG) filter. The choice of DoG filter depends upon the quality of available image and the information content, i.e, the value of blurriness (standard deviation) can be controlled and hence the edges can be highlighted more accurately. From the filtered image, texture statistics are captured using local ternary pattern (LTP) extracted from four different orientation images to form DoGLTP. The different orientations used in this work enable us to capture angle information usually ignored by many pattern-based features. In the proposed feature, color information is included through Hue and Saturation histograms. This makes the proposed feature more robust and the retrieval results highlight its superior performance in comparison to existing techniques on two popular databases: Corel 1000 and Corel 10k.

articleTitle: Study of GPS C/No ratio for retrieval of Surface Soil Moisture
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, soil moisture retrieval algorithm has been developed utilizing Global Positioning System (GPS) C/No data for bare soil surfaces. The developed algorithm relies on the multipath carrier to noise ratio (C/No) recorded by the receiver. Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System (IRNSS) receiver was used to collect the multipath GPS data from bare soil. Change in C/No was analyzed with elevation angle and it was observed that low elevation angles are suitable for estimation of soil moisture. An empirical relationship was developed between soil moisture and amplitude of fitted C/No data. This developed relationship can be utilized to retrieved soil moisture with GPS C/No data. Obtained results were compared with the soil moisture retrieved with Gravimetric method. Good agreement was observed between the soil moisture retrieved through Gravimetric method and soil moisture retrieved through developed relationship with GPS C/No data.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Diamond Shaped Substrate Integrated Waveguide CSRR Band Pass Filter for X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, compact substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) band pass filters (BPFs) incorporated with novel diamond shaped complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) are proposed and analyzed using simulation software HFSS. First single stage SIW BPF is analyzed with face to face orientation of outer ring. Thereafter, a two stage filter is analyzed with similar type of orientation. The filters are simulated using substrate material RT Duroid 5880 with relative permittivity of 2.2 and height 0.508 mm. The proposed two stage SIW BPF exhibits highly selective pass band with center frequency of 8.86 GHz with 3-dB bandwidth of 0.74 GHz. It also exhibits one stop band with rejection peak below -60 dB in close proximity to two transmission poles in the pass band. The two stage SIW filter has better selectivity, bandwidth and stop band performance.

articleTitle: Real Time Safety Alert System for Car
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Driver's lethargy is one of the main causes of car accidents nowadays. We have discussed fatigue, object detection in hand, head pose estimation and siesta detection. This paper is focused on extracting and analyzing the various factors to alert the driver while driving the car. We have implemented real time face detection by using CNN. We have used light forbearance model as it will be easy to implement in real time situation. Eye tiredness by calculating percentage of eyelid closure over the pupil (PERCLOS), object detection in hand by tensor flow. Object is detected when the driver uses mobile phone and/or holds substance abuse material while driving. Mouth geometric movement detection is implemented by Deep Neural Network. This aims to reduce road accidents and the loss of life. In every 25 second a person dies in road accidents. We have proposed a method to reduce accidents by implementing certain factors. This will alert us whether or not the driver is in the proper condition for driving.

articleTitle: Speaker Identification Based Proxy Attendance Detection System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Recently, voice biometrics has gained popularity due to its large number of applications. The paper presents Siamese Network and CIFAR network-based architecture for speaker identification. It uses the voice metrics and voice features independent of the uttered words. The model is trained on a dataset containing hundreds of audio clips of 10 speakers. The model achieved a test accuracy of 88% and training accuracy of 98.5%. The proposed model is used for proxy attendance detection in the classroom.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of 6T SRAM on 130 nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: CMOS devices are being scaled down for better performance in areas like power dissipation, speed, size and reliability. It is important to reduce the energy usage while increasing the access-time speed, to encourage the growth of memory technology. SRAM finds extensive applications in system-on-chip (SOC) designs. Though various other topologies have been proposed in literature, the core of this paper reviews the standard 6T SRAM bitcell and provides a systematic insight into the structure and analysis techniques using 130nm CMOS technology node. The functioning of the cell has been studied through basic operations like read, write and hold. Static noise margins for read, write and hold operations have been measured from the Voltage Transfer Characteristics and N-curve. Comparisons have also been made between the butterfly curve and N-curve to measure noise margins through simulations. The write noise margin has been further studied through methods like Bitline and Wordline Sweep.

articleTitle: Future Battlefield Air Space Management: An Internet of Things (IoT) Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Future Battlefield has been visualized as a complex process of tactical information exchange among various coordinating units that are participating in the war. In all the three domains of Navy, Air force and Infantry battlefield, the most potent warfare options reside with Air force. There has to be coordination among the above-mentioned domains so that there is limited collateral damage and the enemy suffers heavy causalities. The current paper visualizes a scenario where the Infantry soldiers on the ground are on the move to capture enemy vital assets with the help of coordinated air attacks. To coordinate with the ground realities and air assets, the top priority of Airspace Management (ASM) remains the conflict detection and conflict resolution. Currently, the airspace has become crowded with the traditional aircraft and advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV). This requires closer coordination between the participating entities in the war zone. To support such decision support systems, we propose a novel solution to integrate the Internet of Tings (IoT) devices with battlefield devices. In this paper, we describe the motivation and a theoretical framework of an IoT based system that attempts to automate aspects of Future Battlefield Airspace Management (FBAM). Also, we propose a novel conflict detection algorithm which takes in to account the static and dynamic ground establishments. Further, this FBAM is responsible for conflict detection in flights with different geometrical analysis. These conflicts are sent to the concerned ground establishments using the IoT based hierarchical architecture. Finally, the data collected from the IoT based nodes in the FBAM is used to resolve conflicts and assist the decision support systems.

articleTitle: Performance of Multiplierless FIR Filter based on CSD and Binary: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative study of binary and CSD representation forms on filter coefficients has been presented for acute justification of their selection for designing multiplierless finite impulse response (FIR) filter. For this purpose, a well-known computationally efficient nature-inspired cuckoo search optimization algorithm (CSA) is exploited for optimization perspective. An objective function is constructed to minimize the mean square error of designed filter to its ideal response, and it has been observed that the least number of adders and signed power of two terms (SPTs) are acquired when CSD representation is used.

articleTitle: Despeckle and Segmentation of Carotid Artery for Measurement of Intima-media Thickness
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: B-mode ultrasound images of carotid artery are used to measure the intima-media thickness (IMT), which detects the probabilities of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular diseases. Ultrasound images suffer from peculiar phenomena which creates speckle (a type of noise) on the image. The speckles present in the medical images detoriates the quality of the image. Thus the paper presents a method of removing these speckles by using local statistics mean variance (lsmv) filter. It is a preprocessing step of medical image processing. Conventional IMT was done by locating the far walls of the carotid artery. This can be changed by applying segmentation algorithm which could automatically detect the far walls and could measure the IMT. This paper approaches towards automatic edge detection method using prewitt operator. The performance analysis of the proposed method is done in case despeckling as well as segmentation method. The performance parameters show that the proposed method performs better and at the same time reduces the manual effort.

articleTitle: A Real Time Sign Language Interpretation of forearm based on Data Acquisition Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The popularity of the field of electromyography has reached at a height in the past few years. There are several factors that contribute to the achievement of such a height like sensor technology advancement, exponential rise of computational abilities of computer, progress in understanding of human body and increasing awareness of benefits of interdisciplinary studies. The posture and orientation are the key for the identification of the EMG signal. Sign language is based on the use of specific sign or gesture. Individual sign has three components i.e. shape of hand, movement and location of hand. Multiple signs can be identified with different postures and orientation. This paper presents the fundamental concepts of analog to digital data acquisition with the goals of recording better quality of EMG signals generated by the posture and orientation of muscles of hands. In this paper, a wireless and wearable multi sensor EMG system is developed to translate sign language into spoken language for the dumb, so that they can convey their message through sign to the person who don't know sign language by converting it into spoken form. The paper gives the introduction of EMG, calculation of mean absolute value by short time analysis, knowledge of sensors method and experimental setup along with the scope of EMG and result of the experiment and the recordings obtained.

articleTitle: TagStack: Automated System for Predicting Tags in StackOverflow
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Stack Overflow is one of the popular online media for the programmers to share their knowledge and experience. Developers seeks help from online communities such as Stack Overflow. The objective of our research is to ease the tagging of questions on Stack Overflow. This work proposes TagStack system, a machine learning and feedback-based framework for predicting tags on Stack Overflow. We perform experiment on real world and publically available dataset, and results shows that TagStack system is effective in predicting tags on Stack Overflow.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Min-Max Neural Network based Classification of Histopathology Images
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Classification of histopathology images can provide support towards diagnosis of breast cancer. In this study, a Fuzzy Min-Max (FMM) network based approach is studied and used to classify the magnification independent breast cancer histopathology images. Gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) is used to extract the features from images, and are then feed into FMM network to classify the dataset. BreaKHis database is used in this work, which contains microscopic benign and malignant breast tumor images at four different magnifying factors. Experimental results show that the magnifying factor of 200× gives better recognition rate than other magnification rates.

articleTitle: PAPR Analysis of IFFT and DWT Based OFDM-IM System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) with index modulation (IM) is a recently developed modulation technique in which information is conveyed by the active subcarrier indices and constellation symbols. OFDM-IM offers many advantages but still, it suffers from the problem of high peak to average power ratio (PAPR). In this paper, the PAPR performance of OFDM-IM technique for inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) and Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is shown. Besides, the simulations are also shown for PAPR of OFDM-IM based on look-up table logic. The simulation results show better PAPR performance for DWT OFDM-IM system as compared to the IFFT OFDM-IM system.

articleTitle: Monitoring Harmful Sound Density, Light Intensity State in Industrial Workplace
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Nowadays, Microcontroller has made up the Controlling & detection process very much calmer and feasible too. ATmega328 microcontroller selected here in which is the principal of the control system and also centered on Arduino UNO Platform. In this Paper, using Sound Sensor and Light Depending Resistor to accumulate the sound density and light intensity in a noisy and over intensities of lightened place, and also alerting the property owner and health directorate efficiently and quickly via GSM. Wireless RF transceiver module is used to transmit the processed data and this data is received through the RF receiver and GSM module simultaneously. In conclusion, showing the outcomes of data on 7-segment multi-display and alarming the harmful state of sound and light intensity comparing with the standard data through different colored LEDs. Intended to let it warn when data span away from normal range, we intend to set high and low limit of sound and light intensity through potentiometer.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Light Controller for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In metro cities, the monitoring, organizing and controlling road traffic has become a challenge to make human life easier. A vehicular Ad-Hoc Network (VANET) is a promising research area to reduce the day to day hurdles in traffic flows. It is used to collect and provide the vehicular information such as speed of a vehicle, operational conditions, traffic density, traffic flow and average waiting time etc. to the Traffic Light Controller (TLC) at a four-way intersection. Therefore, safe, simple and cost-effective solutions are required to increase transportation efficiency using VANET. Research on Artificial Intelligence technique e.g. Neuro-fuzzy controller, reinforce learning, evolutionary algorithm and static embedded controller is ongoing to adjust to the traffic-related problems but difficult to implement. We present a Traffic Light Controller (TLC) design to monitor Green Light-time Estimation (GLE) and delay for efficient traffic flow. This Adaptive TLC based on Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) observes current traffic condition around the intersection and controls the traffic signals to obtain efficient traffic flow. This paper compares and presents two approaches of TLC-first approach considers the traffic density and traffic flow rate for estimating green light time. The second approach observes the green light time on the basis of traffic flow rate, queue size, and vehicular communication data before controlling traffic light.

articleTitle: Low-Temperature Reliability of Sub-20nm 4H-SiC Trench MOSFET with Black Phosphorus Gate Material
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper examines the low-temperature reliability of 4H-SiC Trench (4H-SiC-T) MOSFET using Black Phosphorus (BP) gate electrode and results so obtained are simultaneously compared with Conventional Trench (CT) MOSFET. Results show that sub-20nm 4H-SiC-T structure is reliable even when the temperature is very low (100K). 4H-SiC-T-MOSFET shows high performance in terms of lower I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub> (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-19</sup> A), high electric field (2.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> V/cm), higher electron mobility (~1700 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>), improved energy band profiles, surface potential, and lower electron temperature (150K); owing to excellent properties of SiC and amalgamation of black phosphorus onto the trench gate which shows the potential in very low-temperature environment.

articleTitle: Grounded Series R-L impedance Simulator using CDDITA
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The research work proposes a new grounded series R-L impedance simulator employing Current differencing differential input transconductance amplifiers (CDDITAs). The presented circuit consists of two CDDITAs along with single grounded capacitor and single grounded resistor. Some major advantages of proposed design are; (i) All the passive elements used in circuit are grounded. So, circuit is a suitable candidate for on-chip implementation, (ii) The inductive part of the realized impedance is electronically tunable through bias currents, (iii) both Inductive as well as Resistive part are independently tunable (iv) no active and/or passive element matching is required and (v)admirable performance under non-ideal environment. To show the workability and usefulness of the presented configuration a current mode low pass filter (CMLPF) is constructed. All theoretical results are verified by performing simulations under PSPICE environment.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Hexagonal-QAM Signals in Nakagami-mFading Distribution
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: LucaRugini, in 2016, proposesthe symbol error probability (SEP) expression of hexagonal-QAM (HQAM), in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN)and Rayleigh fading channel. In this paper, using the above concept, we propose an approximate yet accurate expressionof the SEP for HQAM signals, in Nakagami-mfading channel. We provide a solution to a definite integral, where the integrand is the product of the square of Gaussian Q function and the probability density function of Nakagami- m fading envelope. The approximate solution of this integral leads to the SEP approximation which remarkably matches with the exact SEP curve andprovidesan improved performance over existing SEP approximations. The proposed SEP approximation simplifies the exact SEP expression and does not limit to only the integerm. In addition, itis accurate for the complete SNR range.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of HgCdTe Infrared Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Design of an Infrared (IR) Optical Detector using the alloy Mercury Cadmium Telluride (HgCdTe) is presented. The proposed structure mainly has three layers, two of them are IR absorbing layers with different cut-off wavelengths while the third layer is sandwiched between the two photosensitive layers to prevent the transfer of carriers across the layers and thus acting as an electrical barrier. The simulation results, depict current densities at different wavelengths, considering both cases of recombination and no-recombination indicate that this detector is suitable for photodetection in the infrared region in two transmission windows, namely mid-wave IR (2-5 μm) and long-wave IR (6-12 μm).

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Photonic Crystal Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper a complete Photonics Crystal based Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser has been designed successfully for optical interconnect applications. This PC-VCSEL is designed with GaAs-based PC-VCSELs to transmit optical data having approximately 850-1060-nm emission wavelengths. Basic design principles that are critically important for the design and development of PC-VCSELs, such as hole diameter, hole depth, distributed Bragg reflectors mirrors composition and many more are considered while designing PC-VCSEL. The results are obtained in form of mode intensity profile and refractive index for photonic crystal cavity in planar view, intricate intensity distribution in the near field and far field projections.

articleTitle: An Epsilon Negative Line Based Dual-Band Metamaterial Inspired Antenna for Low-Profile Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a dual band open-ended metamaterial (MTM) inspired antenna with virtual ground plane is proposed. Zeroth-order resonance (ZOR) and first order resonance (FOR) is originated by means of epsilon negative transmission line. It is designed on a via less coplanar waveguide (CPW) single layer. The presented metamaterial (MTM) antenna shows dual-band characteristics with ZOR at 1.31 GHz and FOR at 2.78 GHz corresponding to 40 MHz and 120 MHz, -10 dB bandwidth respectively. The proposed antenna having dimensions of 25 mm × 22.5 mm × 1.6 mm and electrical dimensions of 0.109λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.098λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>× 0.007λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. Here λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free space wavelength corresponds to f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>= 1.31 GHz. This antenna is showing bipolar radiation pattern in yz- plane whereas monopolar-type radiation pattern in xz- plane. This antenna exhibits radiation efficiencies of 67.07% and 81.43% at first and second band respectively. This antenna has satisfactory radiation characteristics which makes it suitable candidate for radiolocation and satellite applications.

articleTitle: Security Analysis for Mixed RF-FSO system in the presence of a RF - Eavesdropper
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper investigates the secrecy performance for a decode-and-forward (DF) based mixed radio-frequency (RF) and free-space-optics (FSO) cooperative wireless network. The Rayleigh distribution is used to characterize the RF channel, similarly the turbulence effect in the FSO link is characterized by double-generalized-Gamma (DGG) distribution. The effect of pointing error is included during analysis. The closed form expressions of outage-probability for secrecy (SOP) and probability of non-zero secrecy capacity or strictly-positive-secrecy-capacity (SPSC) are analysed in terms of Meijer'G function. Finally all of the aforementioned results are verified via Monte-Carlo simulation.

Index Terms: Simultaneous Wireless Information And Power Transfer

articleTitle: DPSN: A Novel approach for Disease Prediction based on Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Disease prediction has always been challenging and critical research area. A lot of machine learning approaches have been developed in past to address this problem. In this paper a novel approach for disease prediction has been proposed. The approach is based on social network of diseases which is constructed using similarity among patient symptoms. The edges are weighted on the basis of the cosine similarity between the diseases. Social network metrics like degree and closeness centrality are used to predict high probable disease. The proposed method has been compared with existing machine learning approaches. The experimental results show that, when predicting disease from the set of 18 possible diseases with 30 possible symptoms, the proposed technique show better performance than traditional machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Deterministic Millimeter-Wave Channel Modeling Based on Ray-Tracing in Urban Scenario
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mm-wave) propagation is considered as one of the potential candidates for future fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication. This paper presents a ray-based deterministic channel modeling for analysis of mmwave propagation in urban scenario. The proposed model is based on uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) and geometrical optics (GO). Different physical mechanisms like diffraction, diffraction followed by reflection, line-of-sight (LOS), and ground reflection have been used to obtain the total field at receiver (Rx). Considering 28 GHz as the potential band for 5G communication, results for mm-wave propagation have been simulated for both soft and hard polarizations and also have been compared with those for current cellular technologies like second-generation (2G), third-generation (3G), and fourth-generation (4G). The analysis reveals that the total field at Rx gets more attenuated with increase in carrier frequency. Finally, the dependence of field strength on different parameters like Rx position, Rx height has been analyzed.

articleTitle: A Novel Architecture of High Performing Reconfigurable Computer Based on Hack Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: We explore the feasibility of implementing a custom processor on a FPGA. For this purpose we have chosen a simple but powerful computer platform called the Hack computer, which consist of a CPU, data memory, instruction memory and memory map I/O controllers. The CPU is small and it fits in about 400 LEs of our FPGA.

articleTitle: Anomalous Ozone Measurements Detection Using Unsupervised Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Air Quality has become a major area of concern in today's world due to the industries and heavy traffic in urban environments. It is also important to analyze the reason behind the degradation of Air quality to curb further damage and provide appropriate remedial measures. In this context, this paper studies different Machine learning methods to detect Anomalous Ozone Measurements in Air Quality data. The comparative study done using unsupervised Machine learning approaches-One Class Support Vector Machine and Isolation Forests showed that Isolation Forests performed better than One- Class Support Vector Machine. Also, these predicted anomalies were tested for a faulty sensor using Z-Score. Isolation Forest was the most effective in finding anomalies in Ozone measurements from Air Quality sensor data, as compared to One Class Support Vector Machine with an accuracy of 92.7%.

articleTitle: Impact of BOX Thickness Scaling on Channel Modulated Electric Field of DC-EFM FD-SOI MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Incurrent scenario theFD-SOI MOSFET considered as one of the potential candidate for higher electrical performance. This paper presents an analysis of developed channel SOI-MOSFET with electric field modulation (DC-EFM FDSOI) in terms of modulation of electric field, variations of front and back oxide thickness and the parasitic capacitance. The concept of DC-EFM has been introduced in the drain region of conventional FD SOI MOSFET in order to improve its threshold voltage, subthreshold slope and the DIBL and reduces the parasitic capacitance. The threshold voltage and drain currenthas been used to investigate the device and also the results have been compared with the different FD-SOI MOSFETavailable in the literature. The device is designed and simulated using the Sentaurus TCAD device simulator.

articleTitle: Modelling of Graphene Based Tunable Ring Resonator for THz Biosensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The emerging applications of split-ring resonators (SRR) have revolutionized the nano-scale integrated circuit (IC) technology with the goals of confinement and up gradation of applied electromagnetic fields. Graphene based SRR provide tunability in the transmission characteristics with varying values of chemical potential. The tunability feature in graphene based SRR structures can be utilized in THz IC applications. This paper shows graphene SRR biosensor, which can be used for THz frequencies. The in-depth analysis of transmission characteristics have been carried out to visualize the sensing capabilities with the help of full-wave simulations. The proposed nano-device presents some transmission peaks with its applications in switches, modulators, etc.

articleTitle: Fuel Economy Analysis for Vehicular Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Fuel economy standards in United States would require new vehicles to achieve at least 34.1 miles per gallon on average by year 2020. Significant enhancements to existing vehicular system are required to achieve this target. New vehicles must have better engine, drive-type, transmission, and fuel type combination so as to increase the number of vehicles with greater average mileage achieved. These changes will not only increase average mileage, but also reduce fuel usage, and thus reducing its corresponding production energy demands as well. Using XGBoost and Random Forest classifier, a prediction model is proposed to compute Green-House score and combined average mileage, owing to vehicle specific performance parameters.

articleTitle: Localisation of spliced region using pixel correlation in digital images
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Image forgery has become the main concern of the society over the past many years due to an increase in the number of false cases of image manipulation leaving a severe impact on the life of a victim. Therefore, it has become necessary to solidly build forgery detection method to overcome image forgery problem. This necessity led to research in this field of image processing and provide detection techniques to check the integrity of images. In this paper, a method for localization of such tampered region is proposed. The proposed method uses unsupervised learning approach to localize the region of image and find whether the region is forged or not. It uses GLCM, a textural feature descriptor that uses pixel correlation in image to extract features from it. Further, for feature matching, Euclidean and Hellinger distance is used and finally, the localization of tampered region is performed. Euclidean and Hellinger distance is calculated separately on each image for comparison of the results. The experimental results showed that Hellinger outperformed Euclidean distance in feature matching and gave better localization results.

articleTitle: Comparative Design and Analysis of FinFET and CMOS SRAM Cell
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: FinFET technology has allayed various important challenges associated with the scaling of conventional CMOS transistors. Due to its many predominant attributes, especially in the area of performance, low voltage operation, leakage power and significantly lower control voltage for SRAMs, FinFETs are thus substituting conventional CMOS as the device of choice. Hence, they prove to be a promising alternative to resolve problems due to short channel effects faced in conventional MOSFETs. In this paper, we have analyzed the performance of SRAM cell circuits implemented using CMOS transistors and FinFETs. FinFETs have been compared to CMOS transistors on the basis of read and write delay incurred in 6T SRAM cell. The read failure susceptibility in FinFET and CMOS based 6T SRAM cell has also been studied in the paper. In the industry, it is also important for the transistors to have a good noise threshold. Thus, the static noise margin for both Finders' and CMOS in a respective 6T SRAM cell has also been studied.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Multilabel Classifiers on Software Engineering Q&A Community for Tag Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the paper, we are analyzing and classifying the tags of the textual content of Software Engineering, Stack Exchange Q&A website by using text pre-processing and classification algorithm. These methods were chosen because the tags provided by the dataset were too general to contextualize the questions. Further the selected classification methods are being compared using accuracy, and used to predict the tags correctly. The accuracy found for LinearSVM is the highest among all the classifiers. The tags predicted by LinearSVM has given the best results of 96% as its ROC score.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization of IEEE 802.15.3c mm-Wave Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: 60 Ghz spectrum is known to be potential frequency spectrum for 5G technology. Some suggested channel to investigate 60 GHz wireless networks. In this paper, we study the channel behaviour and propagation characteristics of IEEE 802.15.3c model for differnt environments such as delay spread, antenna gain and power delay profile. mathematical modeling and Monte-carlo simulation have also been carried out.

articleTitle: Characterization of Wall Parameters using Insertion Transfer Function Method in ‘Through-the-Wall’ Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The wall parameters namely, dielectric constant, attenuation constant and loss tangent have been calculated using insertion transfer function method. These parameters have been calculated with through-the-wall imaging (TWI) for three different types of walls. Experimental data has been collected by using A, B and C scanning. The experimental set up is created by connecting a vector network analyzer (VNA) to a computer in order to operate it as Step Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) radar. The data processing has been done using Mathworks<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> MAT LAB (R2013a) and National Instruments-Virtual Instrument Software Architecture (NI-VISA). All the calculations have been carried out in operating frequency range of 2 to 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Conformal Slot Antenna for Hyperthermia Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a new compact conformal slot antenna having the highly focused beam which is in close proximity with muscle medium is presented for hyperthermia application. A simple 50 Ω microstrip line is used to excite the proposed conformal antenna. The input reflection coefficient of the antenna and hyperthermia assurance parameters viz. penetration depth, effective field size and temperature distributions in the muscle medium are evaluated for different antenna curvature (curvature of the applicator is alike to the bio-model). The simulation study reveals the effectiveness of the proposed antenna for hyperthermia treatment of abdominal tumors.

articleTitle: Electrical and Optical Characteristics of MoOx/ZnO Based Thin Film Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work reports the optical characteristics of MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/ZnO thin films based ultra-violet (UV) photodetector. The substrate used for the fabrication of UV detector is p-Si over which a thin film of Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (150 nm) is deposited. Photoactive layer of ZnO thin film (100 nm) is deposited epitaxially over the Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> using spin coating technique. At the top of solution processed ZnO thin film MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (25 nm) is deposited. Aluminum is used as a top (50 nm) and bottom (80 nm) electrode deposited using thermal evaporation. The fabricated device forms a junction between MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and ZnO which is characterized under the monochromatic UV light (650, μW at 365 nm). Th achieved responsivity of the device is 2.33 A/W. Further, the thin film of the ZnO is analyzed for optical characteristics and the obtained band gap is 3.31 eV.

articleTitle: Tag Based Answer Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Stack Overflow has undoubtedly become a big trend among the programmers and researchers. The problems or doubts faced by any programmer are put on this forum making it available to many knowledgeable people and hence giving out possibly correct solutions. This paper focuses on Tag based Answer Recommendation System on Stack Overflow. This model follows Topic Modeling methodology wherein two techniques were attempted, i.e., LSA(Latent semantic analysis) and LDA(Latent Dirichlet Allocation). These methods deal with various User Queries to find out the most similar questions from the database and hence, deliver the most valid answers related to the question as output. The results from both the Topic Modeling techniques were analyzed with the help of Cosine Similarity as metrics and hence, we found out that LDA performed better than LSA, thereby giving better and more accurate results.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Self Controlled Irrigation System for Home
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The journey of the sapling to become a plant and a plant to grow into a tree includes different stages, out of which irrigation, is one of the most prior and crucial part of its development. Giving your plant too much water is the biggest issue nowadays. Each species of plant has its own watering requirement and giving the plant too much water can spell disaster. Overwatering severely damage plant and could lead to their overall decline. A dry surface is not always a sign of water need. Your plant is wilting but it looks like it has plenty of water. Disorders like Edema could lead to the building of blister-like areas by absorbing water quickly and can cause the death of the plant. Not only it affects the internal organs of the plant but also it sets the leaves to yellowish color. Also, causes root rot, growths of fungus, Mildew, and other harmful weeds. So, there must be a system which can auto control the level of watering with the help of the timer. Also, examine the surrounding soil whether it needs more water or not. The built-in timer will be set by the operator who will decide that for how long the water regulation is to be performed. Moreover, this mechanism could also be handled wirelessly through our portable smartphones which help the plant with an adequate supply of water as per the user need and the soil requirements.

articleTitle: A Systematic Approach of Hardware Design for Acoustic Reflectometry System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: It is possible to determine the properties of the layered media such as snow, soil etc. using acoustic reflectometry in non-invasive manner. These media normally contain layers that have different physical properties like the amount of moisture, porosity, density, etc. Stratigraphy is useful in areas like determination of the water content of snow, density of soil, etc. Researchers have demonstrated that acoustic techniques which are non-invasive can be used to determine the properties of media layers. However, a systematic hardware design approach for these acoustic techniques is not available in the literature. The approach to determine the required specifications of various components like transmitting and receiving transducers, battery etc. are not discussed in the literature. A complete hardware system design for acoustic reflectometry is presented, in this paper. The each aspect of the design like selection of transducers based of requirements, bandwidth of the probe signal, power requirements etc. has been thoroughly discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Possible Active Elements Transposition and Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The paper mainly exploits the possibility of both current-mode and voltage-mode aspects in the emerging area of signal processing. Transposition is one of the possible approaches of converting a current-mode circuit into a voltage-mode circuit or vice versa. In this paper, the possible transpositions of active elements namely, dual-X current conveyor transconductance amplifier (DXCCTA) and current inverting differential input transconductance amplifier (CIDITA) are explored. Moreover, the applicability of obtained transpose active elements is also presented.

articleTitle: SIW Based Two Layer Slot Ring Antenna for X-Band RADAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The circular slot ring structure is a good candidate to form compact antenna with improved gain. The slot ring antenna has the advantage of improved radiation efficiency due to two radiation edges. When two slot ring antenna are stacked one above the other, it provides gain enhancement due to the coupling between the stacked slot structures. This paper discussed about the antenna which has two layer structure of overlapping slot ring which is placed inside a SIW cavity resonator. The antenna is having a microstrip to SIW transition to feed the structure. The antenna resonates at 10GHz which can find its application for Radar gun working in X band.

articleTitle: Optimization of DDS for Peer To Peer Communication over a Constrained Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The Object Management Group (OMG) standardized Data Distribution Services (DDS) is considered to be one of the best middlewares with maximum number of the Quality of Service (QoS) parameters. DDS works on Publish-Subscribe paradigm utilizing different topics (information about single data) to provide specified services to systems in a distributed environment. The number of topics increases with the number of services. These topics come with their respective overheads which consume the available bandwidth on per topic basis within a network. It becomes more severe in the case of communication over constrained networks. In case of communication over constrained networks, where resources are limited characteristically, the Peer To Peer (P2P) paradigm is chosen. Generally, the choice of communication paradigm of publish-subscribe and P2P are mutually exclusive for any schema. We propose to arrive at an engineering compromise to have the benefits of DDS and P2P. In this paper the design towards hybrid objective of having P2P over DDS is presented. The design caters for synchronous P2P service invocation primitive over DDS. The DDS communication has been optimized for the P2P communication among multiple services while limiting overheads of topics on constrained network. In order to achieve the desired objective we have designed an application logic which is akin to Multiplexing-Demultiplexing.

articleTitle: Morphology based Character Recognition of Overlapped and Touched Objects
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: learning (artificial intelligence); feature extraction; Internet of Things; image texture; pattern classification; data mining; regression analysis; support vector machines; integrated circuit design; Rayleigh channels.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction: A Survey of the Types, Techniques, Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Feature extraction (FE) is an important step in image retrieval, image processing, data mining and computer vision. FE is the process of extracting relevant information from raw data. However, the problem of extracting appropriate features that can reflect the intrinsic content of a piece of data or dataset as complete as possible is still a challenge for most FE techniques. In this paper, we present a survey of the existing FE techniques used in recent times. In this study, it was observed that the most unique features that can be extracted when using GLDS features on images are contrast, homogeneity, entropy, mean and energy. In addition, it was observed that FE techniques are not mainly application specific but can be applied to several applications.

articleTitle: Audio Compression Using a Modified Discrete Cosine Transform with Temporal Auditory Masking
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, audio compression has become a very popular area of research. Today, innovations in audio signal processing are used in numerous applications which include advanced audio coding (AAC), perceptual audio coding schemes (MP3 encoding), internet radio and other lossless audio coding schemes. This paper proposesan algorithm for the compression of audio signals using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) with temporal auditory masking (TAM). Furthermore, we have developed a system for audio data compression and evaluated the proposed algorithm using its compression ratio (CR), peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) and transmission delay (TD). The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm gives a compression ratio (CR) of 4:1 of the original signal. All the simulations are carried out using Octave Signal Processing Tool kit and the codes are written in Octave with C programming language.

articleTitle: Permission based Android Malicious Application Detection using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Since the launch of the smartphones, their usage is increasing exponentially. They have become an important part of our lives. We are very much dependent on smartphones for our daily routine and use numerous applications both from the play store or the third party applications. Most of the times, the applications downloaded from unofficial sources pose a threat as there doesn't exist the necessary checks or mechanisms to validate the authenticity of these applications and maybe infected with malware. The malware infected applications can lead to leakage of user's personal data. Anti-virus tools use signature based methods for detecting malwares, but their databases need to be updated regularly. In this paper, we present a system for classifying Android applications on the basis of permissions used by those applications. We used six machine learning algorithms for classifying these applications into malicious or benign applications. On comparing the results, we find that Logistic Regression Algorithm suits best to our dataset and provide 99.34% accuracy.

articleTitle: Developing a Secure Soldier Monitoring System using Internet of Things and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Currently, a state's army is considered a vital tool for its security. Therefore, tracking and monitoring the health and position of a soldier becomes necessary to ensure their safety. In recent years, a lot of technological advances happen in the field of sensors. One of the popular areas utilizing sensors is developing human healthcare system to monitor vital body signals. The network of such sensors that are used to monitor vital human signal for health care is called Body Sensor Network (BSN). Similarly, a small GPS module can be used to track a person's location. In this paper, we describe a system comprising of a sensor module to be mounted on a soldier's arm for real-time health and position monitoring, which transmits and stores a soldier's data in an encrypted form in a BlockChain; thus making the data tamper proof and distributed. The mounted sensor module consists of a temperature, heart-rate, and GPS module, with 1.15%, 11.1% relative errors in the sensors respectively and 1.62 m, 2.05 m deviation in latitude and longitude of the GPS module in their readings compared against commercial devices. The BlockChain will exist on army controlled computers.

articleTitle: Deployment of Cognitive RF for Performance Enhancement of FSO systems: A FSO/Cognitive RF Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Cognitive Radio has been proposed as an ideal solution for identifying and utilizing the spectral holes in the licensed RF spectrum. Due to FSO's (Free Space Optical) susceptibility to extreme weather conditions like fog, snow etc., a RF link as a backup for the FSO system is a largely accepted solution. Since licensed RF spectrum is scarce, thus, allocating a dedicated RF resource for each FSO link may not be viable. Cognitive Radio can overcome this hurdle. This work investigates the possible role of Cognitive RF as a supporting link for a FSO system. A hybrid FSO/Cognitive RF system is considered in which the FSO system is equipped with a RF transceiver but does not have a dedicated licensed RF resource. Energy detection is used to detect the status of a nearby licensed RF spectrum. Depending on the detected status, the licensed RF is used on a Cognitive basis in `Interweave' mode to form a Hybrid FSO/Cognitive RF system. Performance analysis is presented and closed form expressions are derived for outage probability and RF utilization. The analysis assumes a Gamma-Gamma fading channel for the FSO, Rayleigh fading for the RF sensing channel and Nakagami-m fading for the secondary RF channel. Impact of primary channel occupancy, probability of detection, probability of false alarm and thresholds (optical and RF) have been analyzed. Results show considerable improvement in outage probability over the FSO system with better utilization of the licensed RF resource.

articleTitle: A Study of Adaptive CMOS Circuits Extracting Feature of Neuroplasticity in Human Brain
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Human Brain can learn new things and adapt in new environment. The paper goal is to study learning trends and adaption capability of human brain. The feature of learning, programming and adaption of brain has been emulated using CMOS based circuits. Such circuits can develop devices/chips to recover from traumatic brain injuries, enhance memory abilities; effective learning and can enhance wide range of cognitive abilities of brain. The paper illustrates various CMOS based circuits, like neural firing rate detector, adaptive winner takes all circuit (WTA), time staggered WTA and a bimolecular sensor network. The designs are using Floating gate MOSFET (FGMOS) adaptive model and considered it as a brain synapse (neuron). Post fabrication programming, self-adaption and non-volatile storing capability of FGMOS have been extracted to emulate various such features of human brain. The FGMOS synapse simulation model has also been discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of Supercapacitor for the Development of Energy Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Starch derived activated carbons are prepared at different carbonization temperatures of 700°C, 800 °C and 900°C. Good porous morphology of the prepared activated carbon was found in scanning electron microscopy study. Three supercapacitor cells were fabricated by using the prepared activated carbon as an electrode material and 6M KOH as an electrolyte. Electrochemical testing of the supercapacitor were made by using the well known three techniques as; cyclic voltammetry, Impedance Spectroscopy and charge-discharge. Outcomes of these studies suggested that the activated carbon prepared at 800°C exhibits much better capacitive assets than the other two. Analyzing electrochemical properties of fabricated supercapacitor cells by Impedance Spectroscopy, a lowest bulk resistance 0.231 ohm cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and charge transfer resistance 1.44 ohm cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was found for activated carbon 800°C among all of three. The experimental impedance data were fitted successfully by using theoretical electrical equivalent circuit model of the supercapacitor. For the optimized supercapacitor, the calculated specific capacitance from the cyclic voltammetry method is found 261.3 F g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> at a voltage scan rate of 20 mV s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. By analyzing charge-discharge data the observed specific capacitance was 230.5 F g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and it was correspond to the specific energy and specific power of 17.2 Wh Kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and 983 W Kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, respectively. These outcomes represent the potentiality of the supercapacitor to be used in various microelectronic circuits.

articleTitle: Speech Enhancement for Punjabi Language Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Speech contains sounds that delineate words of a language. Capturing speech in different real environmental circumstances may contain different mixtures of many different sound waves (i.e. the mixture of sounds, noises and other effects like reverberation). Such noisy environments make difficult to capture clear speech and hence degrade the speech quality. Due to the different nature of noise and reverberation effect, it must be necessary to remove extra noise and reverberation effect separately. This paper proposes a hybrid approach that uses various algorithms sequentially to remove noise, reverberation effect, and cocktail party problem. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is representation learning method that uses basis matrix and activation coefficients to produce the basic spectral structure of speech. Deep learning use supervised mapping function to map noisy spectrum to target speech spectrum. NMF with deep learning can jointly be used to separate non-stationary noise from target speech. On other hands, the non-negative convolutive transfer function (nCTF) estimates the coefficient of reverberation. Non-negative convolutive transfer function with NMF can be used to reduce the effect of the room impulse response (RIR). Gaussian mixture model-universal background model (GMM-UBM) extracts the compact representation of speech. GMM-UBM with deep classifier used to extract target speech from cocktail party problem (the mixture of sounds of multiple speakers). The Proposed system is based on the Punjabi language that aims to enhance speech under noisy-reverberant environments and the cocktail party problem.

articleTitle: Fabrication of CZTS Thin Films based Solar Cells using Vacuum Deposition Techniques: A Status Review
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent times, Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>ZnSnS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (CZTS) quaternary compound has attracted significant attention for application in solar cells, due to its suitable direct band gap, high abundance, low cost and low toxicity. Various vacuum and non- vacuum based methods have been adopted for the fabrication of CZTS thin films. Vacuum based methods such as pulse laser deposition and evaporation have the advantage of controlled chemical composition and higher reproducibility. This work reviews the different vacuum based methods for preparation of CZTS thin films present in the literature. The effect of fabrication conditions and preparation methods on film properties has been analyzed. Present status and progress of CZTS thin film solar cells while identifying future path for more efficient device structure has been presented.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Imputation Approaches with Noise Filtration on Medical Data
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Accuracy of any prediction model on the data set which is having large number of missing values is always a challenging problem. The popular technique in order to handle missing values is known as case deletion in which we simply delete the missing instances. Many hybrid models have either used some default way to fill the missing values or case deletion. Concept Most Common (CMC) method has proved best imputation technique in case of Hepatitis data set and Case deletion has performed best in case of Wisconsin Breast Cancer Data, according to literature. The effectiveness of this missing value imputation is heavily dependent on the observed data (or complete data) and that data too contains many imperfections like noise, redundancies etc. So, the objective of this paper is to investigate the effect of performing noise filtration on the imputation task. Specifically, two different procedures for combining instance selection and missing value imputation are proposed and are compared on the basis of their classification accuracy. The results obtained are promising and superior to the recently proposed methods.
